Axiom: A type-system escape hatch — a cast (`as any` / `as unknown` / `as never`, type assertions) or a suppression (`@ts-ignore` / `@ts-expect-error`) — defeats the static guarantees the code relies on. Default: do not use one — model the type properly (narrowing, guards, generics, discriminated unions). When one is genuinely unavoidable it is surfaced and justified in writing, never silent: a documented `@ts-expect-error ` carrying a Decision Log reference (`D-NNN`) that states why it is needed and why the alternatives do not work. A bare cast hides the problem; a documented suppression names it. Enforced mechanically by `CastSafetyCheck` and `DisablesCheck`.
